newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Mexico should copy Argentine parity law - Dornbusch.
newsitem.headline: Mexico should copy Argentine parity law - Dornbusch.

text.p: U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch called Argentina's exchange policy pegging the peso to the dollar "excellent" and urged Mexico to adopt it.
Adressing a bankers conference in Buenos Aires, the Massachussets Institute of Technology economics and management professor also said he thought Brazil's real was overvalued.
"Argentina's exchange system is excellent," he told the meeting, according to an Association of Argentine Banks (ADEBA) communique, which reproduced extracts of his speech.
"Nobody is crazy enough to propose changes. Probably it will not even be necessary to modify it in two, five or 10 years."
Dornbusch said there was a global trend for countries to peg exchange rates to different currencies.
The professor, who correctly predicted the Mexican peso crash of 1994, advised Mexico to catch up with that trend.
"Mexico should do that too, mostly taking into consideration Argentina's experience."
Referring to Brazil, Dorbusch said "the exchange rate in that country is overvalued."
The ADEBA cited Dornbush as saying there there will be no Brazilian devaluation, at least for the time being.
"The only official policy in Brazil is that of the reelection of (President) Fernando Henrique Cardoso," which requires low inflationary levels, he said.

Turning again to Argentina, he said that in the past five years it made "significant progress" to lower its country-risk and that international ratings were not adequately reflecting those achievements.

Referring to Argentina's unemployment of 17.3 percent, Dornbusch said the country's high jobless rate recalled the experience of Chile, "which in 1985 had a 30 percent unemployment rate and in 1991 reached full employment."
"Argentina can be the same (insofar) as no instantenous solutions exist," he added, according to the ADEBA communique.
